16 - Verify selecting a different color swatch updates the selected-color label and swaps the gallery image
Two test-authoring pitfalls caught and fixed here, neither a product defect: (1) the swatches container is `x-defer="intersect"` (Alpine only wires up its bindings once the element intersects the viewport, a deliberate lazy-hydration pattern in this theme) — reading the "selected" label text immediately after navigate, with no settle step first, can race Alpine's hydration and read an empty string; scrolling the swatch into view first (which carries its own built-in ~600ms settle wait in this runner) before the FIRST read, not just before the click, reliably avoids the race. (2) the real color `<input type="radio">` is `z-index:-1` (visually behind its own wrapping `<label>`, which is the genuine clickable surface a real user sees/clicks) — clicking the input directly is unreliable because Playwright's own hit-testing can resolve to the covering label at that point without actually delegating the click back to the input in every case; clicking the wrapping `<label>` itself (the input's own parent element) is both more realistic and 100% reliable across repeated runs. FIXED 2026-09-15 — attribute-label span id updated from attribute-label-2118-93 to attribute-label-2123-93 (this product's own internal id, 2123) after the module's fixture product changed (see file-header note); the default "Gull Grey" / alternate "Pine Green" color pair happens to be identical on this replacement product, so no other change was needed.

16b - [Negative] Verify the selected color swatch shows a real visible highlight ring, not just an internal state change
Confirmed real defect via direct computed-style inspection, matching the client's manual-testing screenshot ("Selected color not keep highlighting" — no swatch ever visibly appears selected). The click handler DOES correctly update internal state (input.checked flips, and the label's class list correctly gains "ring ring-primary/50") and the text label above the swatches correctly updates too (see test 16) — but the Tailwind "ring" utility classes being applied are never actually compiled into this site's CSS bundle: the selected swatch's own computed `box-shadow` is literally "none" despite having the ring classes in its class list, so the highlight has zero visual effect. Distinct from the HOVER outline, which was separately confirmed working correctly (a real blue `outline: 2px solid` appears on :hover via a completely different CSS mechanism/rule) — only the persistent SELECTED-state ring is broken.
Failed ▼
syncing…
# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 After clicking a color swatch, the newly-selected label's computed box-shadow is "none" even though its class list contains "ring ring-primary/50" (and "ring-primary/75" once selected) — confirmed via direct getComputedStyle inspection. The Tailwind ring utility was never compiled into the site's CSS (most likely a JIT/purge content-scan miss on a dynamically-applied class name), so no visible highlight ring ever appears around the selected swatch, matching the client's own screenshot showing all 4 swatches with identical plain borders regardless of which one is actually selected.
⚠ ErrorAfter clicking a color swatch, the newly-selected label's computed box-shadow is "none" even though its class list contains "ring ring-primary/50" (and "ring-primary/75" once selected) — confirmed via direct getComputedStyle inspection. The Tailwind ring utility was never compiled into the site's CSS (most likely a JIT/purge content-scan miss on a dynamically-applied class name), so no visible highlight ring ever appears around the selected swatch, matching the client's own screenshot showing all 4 swatches with identical plain borders regardless of which one is actually selected.
🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG — Tailwind CSS's JIT compiler generates utility classes only for class names it can find as literal strings during its content scan. This theme applies the ring classes conditionally via an Alpine :class binding ('border-gray-100 ring ring-primary/50': (selectedValues[93] === item.id)) — a computed/templated string, not a literal class name anywhere in the scanned source files — so Tailwind's build never generates the corresponding .ring/.ring-primary/50 CSS rules. The class gets applied to the DOM correctly at runtime, but no matching CSS rule exists to render it, so box-shadow computes to "none".
❌ Problematic Code
The Alpine :class binding in the swatch template uses a dynamically
interpolated Tailwind class string that Tailwind's static content
scanner cannot see as a literal token, e.g. :class="{ 'border-gray-100
ring ring-primary/50': (selectedValues[93] === item.id) }".
✅ Fixed Code
Add the literal class strings ("ring", "ring-primary/50",
"ring-primary/75") to Tailwind's safelist in the project's Tailwind
config, OR restructure the binding so the full class strings appear
literally in the template source (Tailwind's scanner only needs to see
the exact string once, anywhere in scanned content, to generate it).
📋 What To Do
1. Add the swatch-selection ring classes to tailwind.config.js's safelist array (or confirm they already appear literally elsewhere in the codebase that Tailwind scans). 2. Rebuild the CSS bundle and re-verify the selected swatch now shows a real visible ring — re-run this test. 3. Audit other Alpine :class-bound Tailwind utility strings in this theme for the same pattern, since this is a systemic risk wherever a class name is only ever assembled dynamically rather than appearing literally in a scanned file.

# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 Across repeated attempts (including this suite's own back-to-back automated runs), clicking "Beli Langsung" while logged in inconsistently lands on /checkout/ or back on the referring product page — confirmed via direct POST-body capture that the correct return_url value is sent every single time, ruling out a client-side cause; the server-side redirect destination is simply not reliable.
⚠ ErrorAcross repeated attempts (including this suite's own back-to-back automated runs), clicking "Beli Langsung" while logged in inconsistently lands on /checkout/ or back on the referring product page — confirmed via direct POST-body capture that the correct return_url value is sent every single time, ruling out a client-side cause; the server-side redirect destination is simply not reliable.
🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG (server-side) — the checkout/cart/add controller action does not reliably honor a submitted return_url POST parameter as the post-add-to-cart redirect target. Standard Magento's own add-to-cart flow normally redirects based on the uenc (URL-encoded referrer) segment baked into the form action URL, with return_url being a custom override this theme added — that override appears to only take effect intermittently, most often losing out to the default uenc-based return-to-referrer behavior.
❌ Problematic Code
Not visible from the front end — the inconsistency lives in the
server-side controller/observer responsible for reading the
`return_url` POST field and deciding the post-add-to-cart redirect,
which does not consistently prioritize it over the default uenc
return-to-referrer logic.
✅ Fixed Code
N/A — requires the server-side add-to-cart redirect logic to
consistently check for and prioritize a non-empty `return_url` POST
field over the default uenc-based behavior. See What To Do.
📋 What To Do
1. Locate the custom observer/plugin handling return_url for this store's add-to-cart controller and confirm whether it's reliably registered/executed (a race with another observer, a caching layer, or a condition that only sometimes matches would all produce this "usually falls back to default" symptom pattern). 2. Reproduce server-side with the exact POST body captured during this investigation to isolate whether it's a timing/caching issue or a logic bug in the observer's condition. 3. Re-run this test repeatedly (not just once) after any fix, since a single clean pass was already misleading earlier in this same investigation. FIXED 2026-09-15 — switched login from STEEL_CUSTOMER2 to STEEL_CUSTOMER: live-reconfirmed STEEL_CUSTOMER2 has no saved address (same gap found and fixed in the Cart module's own test 35), which would otherwise redirect to /customer/address/new/ regardless of this test's own redirect logic — a different bug masking as this one. STEEL_CUSTOMER has a saved address and correctly exercises the real Beli Langsung redirect path.
